newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister denies latest corruption report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister denies latest corruption report.

text.p: Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta described as "absurd and untruthful" a newspaper report published Thursday suggesting he gave a lawmaker a television concession in return for his vote.
"The transcript of the conversation does not contain a single real fact or a concrete accusation," Motta said in a statement. "The facts mentioned are absurd, untruthful and, I would say, surreal."

Newspaper Folha de Sao Paulo Thursday published details of a purported taped conversation allegedly between Ronivon Santiago and an unnamed "Mr X" in which it is suggested Motta offered the lawmaker a television concession.

Earlier this week, Folha published transcripts of other conversations allegedly involving Santiago and fellow congressman Joao Maia who allegedly said that they had also been paid cash to vote in favor of the government's re-election bill.
Santiago Wednesday confirmed it was his voice on the tape but said he was joking when he referred the alleged cash bribes. He has not publicly comment on Folha's story Thursday.
Newspapers quoted Maia as saying he did not take any bribes.
In his statement issued Thursday, Motta said: "The issues which have come up through the declarations are repulsive and must be rigorously investigated and punished if proven,"

The concession cited in the Folha report was issued in May 1996 to a company identified as V&N Imagem & Som Ltda in the town of Senador Guiomard, Acre state, within the government's broadcast concessions program, it said.
Acre is the state where the lawmakers named in the scandal hail from.
Valcy de Souza, the owner of V&N Imagem e Som, told Folha de Sao Paulo, he had no connection with any of the congressmen.
